note: Part B (drawing) is not transcribed: no model answer exists.

questions.text: How many different types of characters appear in the figure given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Go row by row and add a character to a running list only when its shape has not been seen before. The 49 Hebrew-style characters reduce to 21 distinct shapes. Watch the near twins: the plain alef and the tilted alef, the closed final mem and the mem with a dot, and pe with a dot against final pe are each counted as different types.

questions.text:
Given below is a series of numbers. Which number will replace the question mark?

101, 103, 107, 109, ?, 127, 131, 137, 139, 149, 151, 157, 163
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Every number in the series is a prime, listed in order. The primes after 109 are 113 and then 127, so the missing number is 113.

questions.text: How many lines are there in the image given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Count line ends instead of lines, because crossings make lines easy to double count. Going round the figure there are 44 free ends, and each straight line has two ends, so there are 44 / 2 = 22 lines.

questions.text: How many configurations of blocks appear only once in the figure given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Each block is a T of four squares, so a configuration is its outer colour together with its centre colour. List every block and tick off repeats: pink with a purple centre, blue with a purple centre, orange with a black centre and yellow with a green centre each appear twice. Every other configuration appears once, and there are 12 of them.

questions.text: What is the number of fonts used in the words given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Sort the words by the shapes of their letters, not by size: compare serifs, the contrast between thick and thin strokes, the ends of strokes and letters such as a, g and e. A word in the same design at a different weight counts with its family only if its letters are built the same way. IIT Bombay's final key gives 6 fonts.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of whole cuboids of length = 2 cm, breadth = 1 cm and height = 1 cm that can be packed into a larger cuboid of length = 3 cm, breadth = 3 cm and height = 11 cm?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The big box holds 99 unit cubes and each small cuboid fills 2 of them, so at most 49 fit. Colour the unit cubes like a 3D chessboard: there are 50 of one colour and 49 of the other, and each cuboid covers one of each, so 49 is the limit. It is reached by standing cuboids upright in the bottom 3 x 3 x 10 part (9 columns of 5 = 45) and laying 4 flat in the top 3 x 3 x 1 layer, giving 49.

questions.text: Prof. Paittiyam, in an attempt to create the world’s most delicious dish, managed to merge a cylindrical Idli (diameter = 17 cm, height = 6 cm) with a torus shaped medu wada (inner hole diameter = 2 cm, outer diameter = 16 cm, and tube diameter i.e height of torus = 7 cm) such that the medu wada is parallel to the base of the Idli and the centeroids of the two solids coincide. How many surfaces does the resulting solid contain?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The wada's outer radius (8 cm) is less than the idli's radius (8.5 cm), so it stays inside the curved side, but its height (7 cm) is more than the idli's (6 cm), so a ring of the wada sticks out 0.5 cm above and below. On top, that ring splits the flat face into an outer flat annulus and an inner flat disc, with the curved ring between them: 3 surfaces. The bottom is the same: 3 more. Add the curved side of the idli: 3 + 3 + 1 = 7.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of equilateral triangles (side 3 cm) that can be placed in a square of side 6.8 cm without overlapping each other?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Laid in straight rows, only two rows of three fit, giving 6, because a row of four needs 7.5 cm. The triangles need not sit in rows: tilting them at different angles lets 8 non-overlapping triangles fit inside the 6.8 cm square. The area limit is 46.24 / 3.9, about 11, but 9 could not be fitted, so the maximum taken is 8.

questions.text: How many triangles are there in the figure shown below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Name the 11 points (the four corners, the centre, the two crossing points on the vertical diagonal and the four points on the sides) and the 10 straight lines through them. A triangle is any three points joined pairwise by drawn lines that do not all lie on one line. Checking every triple of points this way gives 40 triangles, including the large ones that span both halves.

questions.text: Count the number of stacked triangular pieces in the image shown below.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Seen from above, the stack is a large triangle split into 9 small triangular columns (6 pointing one way, 3 the other). Count the layers in each column from its top face down to the ground, using the 6 layers of the tall front left column as a ruler. The back row reads 6, 5, 7, 6, 8, the middle row 4, 3, 5 and the front corner 2, so the total is 32 + 12 + 2 = 46.

questions.text: Shown below is a combination of fixed pulleys. If the triangular load moves down, how many pulleys will rotate in the same direction as the smallest pulley (including itself)? The overlapping paths do not interfere with each other.
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Follow the single rope from the load to the hanging dot through all 23 pulleys. At each pulley note which side the rope runs over: a rope moving right along the top or down the right side turns the pulley clockwise, and the opposite sides turn it anticlockwise. This gives 12 pulleys turning one way and 11 the other. The smallest pulley (left of centre, below the second pulley on the rope) is in the group of 11, so the answer is 11.

questions.text: The current time is 10 minutes past 3 in the afternoon. What will the angle be between the hour hand and the minute hand of the clock, 4 hours and 40 minutes from now?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: 4 hours 40 minutes after 3:10 is 7:50. The minute hand is at 50 x 6 = 300 degrees. The hour hand is at 7 x 30 + 50 x 0.5 = 235 degrees. The angle between them is 300 minus 235 = 65 degrees.

questions.text:
The word ‘Ape’ is an anagram of ‘Pea’. How many of the following words are anagrams of animals?

Glow, flow, loin, sit, balm, bare, god, lane, act, tab, bit, tar, reef
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Rearrange each word: flow is wolf, loin is lion, balm is lamb, bare is bear, god is dog, act is cat, tab is bat and tar is rat. Glow, sit, lane, bit and reef do not rearrange into an animal. So 8 words are anagrams of animals.

questions.text: Privacy of a space depends on the level of closure it has from its surroundings i.e. the difficulty of accessing that space from outside the house. The figure below shows the plans of four houses at a village street junction. Which is the most private room amongst all the rooms across all the houses?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Measure privacy by how many doorways you must pass through from outside to reach a room. In the bottom right house, room 22 opens to the outside, 23 is reached only through 22, 24 only through 23, and 25 only through 24, so room 25 is four doorways deep. Every room in the other houses is at most two doorways from outside, so room 25 is the most private.

questions.text: The figure below shows the layout plan of the conservative Themmalwadi village which consists of a cluster of houses. Black lines represent walls and the openings in those walls represent either windows or doors. Also marked are the houses of Riya (who lives with her family) and Barkya, who are in love and having an affair. So, hidden from the eyes of the villagers, they regularly meet at night in Barkya’s house. Themmalwadi is so conservative that even the sight of women on the street at night raises eyebrows. If Riya takes the path that has the least number of openings, what is the number of openings that she will have to pass by to get to Barkya’s house?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Riya leaves by the door on the left of her house and walks up street A to W, along W, up past T, across to the open area near R, and up to Barkya's door at Z. On the way she passes one opening on W street (in the house above it), one opening in the house at T, and one opening facing the open area near R. Routes through V, J, K or along the top past H and S pass more openings, so the least is 3.

questions.text: Shown in the figure is a pyramid with a square base, formed by vertices EFGH and a top vertex I. The diagonally opposite vertices, EG and FH are connected to form the vertex J at their intersection. The vertices I and J are also connected as shown. How many triangles are formed by all these vertices?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: There are 6 points, E, F, G, H, I and J, and every pair of them is joined by a drawn line (base edges, slant edges, both diagonals through J, and IJ). So any 3 points make a triangle unless they lie on one straight line. There are 20 ways to choose 3 of 6 points, and only E, J, G and F, J, H lie on a straight line, so there are 20 minus 2 = 18 triangles.

questions.text: The length and breadth of the white rectangle are 6 and 4 respectively. The proportions of the outer black, middle red and inner white rectangles are the same. What is the length of the hypotenuse of triangle ABC?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: All rectangles have length : breadth = 3 : 2. The green triangle spans the red rectangle's top edge and meets its bottom at the middle, and the white rectangle's lower corners touch its sides. If the red height is h, its width is 1.5h and at depth 4 the half width is 3, so 0.75h minus 3 = 3, giving h = 8 and width 12. The yellow triangle does the same for the black rectangle, passing through the red top corners: 0.75H minus 6 = 6, so H = 16 and width 24. Triangle ABC has legs 12 and 16, so its hypotenuse is 20.

questions.text: Meethapur works on a barter system. Each person there loves different sweets. Mukund is willing to exchange 2 toffees for a lollypop and 3 ice creams for a toffee. Ranjana is willing to exchange one ice cream for 2 lollypops and 3 toffees for a lollypop. Mukund and Ranjana don’t know each other, but both of them know Sita who loves toffees. Sita has one lollypop. She can meet Ranjana and Mukund only once (not necessarily in that order). What is the maximum number of toffees that Sita can get?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Meet Mukund first: trade the lollypop for 2 toffees, then trade each toffee for 3 ice creams, giving 6 ice creams. Then meet Ranjana: each ice cream fetches 2 lollypops, so 6 ice creams give 12 lollypops, and each lollypop fetches 3 toffees, giving 36 toffees. Meeting Ranjana first gives only 3 toffees, so the maximum is 36.

questions.text: Atul has nine cats that always fight with each other. He puts all of them into a square box. What is the least number of square partitions he must use to keep all the cats separated from each other? You may use any size of square partitions.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The cats sit in a 3 x 3 grid. Place one square partition tilted at 45 degrees with its corners at the midpoints of the box's sides: this cuts off the four corner cats in the four corner triangles. Inside it, place a second, upright square around the centre cat with its corners touching the tilted square's sides: this leaves four triangles, one for each edge cat, and the centre cat alone in the middle. So 2 partitions are enough.

questions.text: How many differences are there in the two images shown below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Compare the two pictures region by region, from one corner across to the other, and note every change: a missing or added object, a change of colour, shape or direction. A change to one face (the left man's moustache and eyes) counts as one difference. IIT Bombay's final key gives 10 differences.

questions.text: On the left is a photograph. Which option(s) is/are part(s) of that photograph?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: Match each square crop against the photograph at the same scale. B is the leaves at the top, C is the pink flowers and stems in the upper middle, and D is the bright leaves at the lower right. A shows a leaf and branch arrangement that does not occur anywhere in the photograph, even when turned or flipped.

questions.text:
If spaces and special characters are ignored in the following text, which country/countries is/are hidden in the text shown below?

I think the earth’s ecosystem will collapse very soon. Natural resources have been exploited for far too long at the cost of the wellbeing of humankind, I am afraid.  I don’t want to stir another controversy but I ardently feel that the time has come for us to take urgent actions to save our planet from manmade disasters.
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Join the letters together. 'humankind I am' gives humank-INDIA-m, which hides India, and 'stir another' gives st-IRAN-other, which hides Iran. Ghana and Peru do not appear as a run of letters anywhere in the text.

questions.text:
The CBI is investigating a dangerous gang of three criminals. The criminals are Donga, Tirudan and Daaku. The investigation team consists of Pradyuman, Daya, Fredricks, Salunkhe, Tarika and Purvi. Each criminal is to be investigated by exactly two investigators, and each investigator investigates exactly one criminal. The investigation is to be conducted subject to the following constraints:

Pradyuman and Daya do not investigate the same criminal.

Fredricks and Salunkhe investigate the same criminal.

If Fredricks investigates Tirudan, then Tarika must investigate Daaku.

Given these constrains, which of the following could be the acceptable assignment(s) of investigators to potential criminals?

options.label: A
options.text: Fredricks & Salunkhe investigate Tirudan, Pradyuman & Daya investigate Donga and Tarika & Purvi investigate Daaku

options.label: B
options.text: Fredricks & Salunkhe investigate Donga, Tarika & Pradyuman investigate Tirudan and Daya & Purvi investigate Daaku

options.label: C
options.text: Tarika & Purvi investigate Donga, Fredricks & Pradyuman investigate Tirudan and Salunkhe & Daya investigate Daaku

options.label: D
options.text: Daya & Purvi investigate Tirudan, Tarika & Pradyuman investigate Daaku and Fredricks & Salunkhe investigate Donga

questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Test each option against the three rules. A puts Pradyuman and Daya together, which is not allowed. C splits Fredricks and Salunkhe, which is not allowed. B and D keep Fredricks with Salunkhe on Donga and keep Pradyuman and Daya apart, and the third rule does not apply because Fredricks is not on Tirudan, so both are acceptable.

questions.text: If, 9 + 8 means 9 is the child of 8, and 7 * 6 means that 6 is the wife of 7, then which of the following statements can be derived from 2 + 3 * 1 + 4 * 5?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Read it in pairs: 2 is the child of 3, 1 is the wife of 3, 1 is the child of 4, and 5 is the wife of 4. So 1 is a woman, the daughter of 4 and 5, and the mother of 2, which makes 2 the grandchild of 4. 5 is a woman (the wife of 4) and is the mother-in-law of 3, not a grandfather. A, B and D follow.

questions.text:
30 circles are given below, with a set of rules:

1. The bigger the circle, the farther away it is from us.

2. The thinner the line of the circle, the closer it is to us.

3. The red circles are farther away from us as compared to the blue circles.

Which of the options given below is/are TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: Circle 25 is the closest to us

options.label: C
options.text: Circle 24 is closer to us than circle 14

options.label: D
options.text: Circle 6 is closer to us than circle 8

questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Circle 25 is blue (closer than any red), the smallest blue circle and drawn with a thin line, so every rule puts it closest to us: A is true and B is false. Circles 24 and 14 are both red with similar lines, and 24 is smaller, so 24 is closer: C is true. Circle 6 is blue like 8 but larger and drawn with a much thicker line, so 6 is farther than 8: D is false.

questions.text: Which concept does this image by Escher illustrate?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The print is Escher's Day and Night. The black and white birds fit together with no gaps, which is tessellation, and the white birds against the dark sky and the black birds against the light sky swap roles as shape and background, which is figure and ground. Mise en scene is a film term for arranging a scene for the camera, and a collage is made by gluing together pieces of different materials, so neither fits.

questions.text:
Read the passage given below, written by Nick Hughes:

“We tend to treat power as though it is intrinsically valuable. We seek it out and covet it, quite irrespective of how we might wield it and what it might get us. One need only look at the history of totalitarian politics to recognise this tendency in its most grotesque form. But power isn’t intrinsically valuable, it’s only instrumentally valuable – valuable as a means to an end. And whether or not they are objectively valuable, the ends that matter to us, the things that we care about most – our relationships, our projects and goals, our shared experiences, social justice, the pursuit of knowledge, the creation and appreciation of art, music and literature, and the future and fate of ours and other species – do not depend to any considerable extent on our having control over a vast but largely irrelevant Universe. We might be distinctly lacking in power from the cosmic perspective, and so, in a sense, insignificant. But having such power and such significance wouldn’t make much of a difference anyway. To lament its lack and respond with despair and nihilism is merely a form of narcissism. Most of what matters to us is right here on Earth.”

Which of the statements is/are TRUE of the paragraph above:

options.label: A
options.text: The author argues that intrinsic value is distinct from instrumental value and that power possesses the latter of the two.

options.label: B
options.text: “Humans and our significance in the universe”, is one of the themes discussed in the passage.

options.label: C
options.text: The philosophies of nihilism and narcissism are suggested as remedies by the author.

options.label: D
options.text: The author suggests that we look at the history of totalitarian politics to recognise that we shun power in the most grotesque form.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: The author says power is not intrinsically valuable but only instrumentally valuable, so A is true. The passage discusses our lack of power and significance from the cosmic view, so B is true. Despair and nihilism are criticised as a form of narcissism, not offered as remedies, so C is false. Totalitarian politics is cited as the most grotesque form of seeking power, not shunning it, so D is false.

questions.text: Which option(s) is/are simple rotations of the figure given below?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Read each ring's colours clockwise and check that all the rings turn by the same amount. In D the outer ring, the dark green, maroon and pink ring, the ring with yellow, red and blue, and the centre all line up with one rotation, so D is a rotation. In A the outer two rings match one rotation but the yellow, red and blue ring matches a different one. B has the outer colours in reverse order, a mirror image. C has two blue pieces in its third ring, so it is a different figure.

questions.text:
Read the statements below:

All female and male natives in their country are strong.
Some men in their country are migrants.
All migrants in their country are not strong.
Not all migrants are women.

Based on the above, which conclusion(s) stated in the options is/are valid?

options.label: A
options.text: Some women in their country are strong.

options.label: B
options.text: Some migrants in their country are men.

options.label: C
options.text: Some people in their country are not strong.

options.label: D
options.text: All strong people in their country are women.

questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Female natives are strong, so some women (the female natives) are strong: A follows. 'Some men are migrants' turns round to 'some migrants are men': B follows. Those migrants exist and no migrant is strong, so some people are not strong: C follows. Male natives are also strong, so not every strong person is a woman: D fails.

questions.text: Which of the following words are similar in meaning?
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: To scribble and to doodle both mean to draw or write carelessly and aimlessly. Nibble means to take small bites and feeble means weak, so neither matches.

questions.text: Which of the following words is/are similar in meaning to ‘Centre’?
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Heart, core and nucleus all name the central part of something. Nub also means the central point or crux (the nub of the matter). So all four are similar in meaning to centre.

questions.text:
Consider this poem:

Now, marriages happen in halls
They used to happen at home
Honeymoon too
Before they wandered into halls
Stage. Actors. Audiences from afar.
Receptions never really took place
Yet they would go on for days.
Now, receptions include
Those who don’t really figure.
Show face, shove envelope (gifts not accepted)
Grin for the camera.
Get out. Not all that bad.
Quick and efficient. No one really cares.

Which mood(s) does the poem evoke?
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Lines like 'Show face, shove envelope' and 'No one really cares' mock today's hollow receptions, which is cynicism. Recalling how weddings 'used to happen at home' and went on for days is nostalgia. Nothing in the poem is joyful or about desire, so happiness and lust do not fit.

questions.text: Goethe said, “Doubt grows with knowledge”. From this perspective, who would a knowledgeable person be?

options.label: A
options.text: One for whom doubt does not grow with knowledge

options.label: D
options.text: One whose doubt grows with knowledge

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: If doubt grows with knowledge, a person with more knowledge has more doubt. So a knowledgeable person is one who has doubt (C) and one whose doubt grows with knowledge (D). A and B contradict the quote.

questions.text:
Theory is already existing knowledge and Practice is knowledge that comes by ‘doing’.

Based on this statement which of the following is/are TRUE?

options.label: D
options.text: Theory and Practice are one and the same.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Theory already exists before anything is done, so it comes before practice (A). Practice is knowledge gained by doing, that is knowledge in action (B). Knowledge that does not come from doing is the already existing kind, theory (C). The statement defines the two differently, so D is false.

questions.text: Which of the following quotes celebrate(s) technology?

options.label: A
options.text: “Did that search engine really know what you want, or are you playing along, lowering your standards to make it seem clever?”

options.label: B
options.text: “ I fear that we are beginning to design ourselves to suit digital models of us, and I worry about a leaching (leakage) of empathy and humanity in the process”

options.label: C
options.text: “The approach to digital culture I abhor would indeed turn all the world’s book into one book”.

options.label: D
options.text: “What a computer is to me is the most remarkable tool that we can ever come up with. It’s the equivalent of a bicycle for our minds”.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Only D praises technology, calling the computer a bicycle for our minds. A doubts search engines, B fears losing empathy to digital models, and C says the speaker abhors one approach to digital culture.

questions.text: Consider the drip irrigation system in villages on hilly terrain. Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Bamboo pipes can be used to divert perennial springs on the hilltops to the lower reaches by gravity.

options.label: B
options.text: If the bamboo pipes have to cross a road they can be taken above the land.

options.label: C
options.text: This irrigation system is useful for the places with high ground water level.

options.label: D
options.text: The bamboo pipes could be replaced with PVC pipes.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: In hill bamboo drip irrigation, spring water from the hilltop is led down through bamboo pipes by gravity (A). Where the line meets a road it can be carried overhead on supports (B). PVC pipes can do the same job as bamboo (D). The system exists to bring water to slopes where ground water is hard to reach, so C is wrong.

questions.text: Six pacmen have joined hands to take revenge from an evil ghost. They are standing around in a circular formation. Lo and behold, a white star full of pure light emerges in the centre. In complete disbelief, the pacmen are mesmerized. Which of the gestalt laws of perception explain(s) the appearance of the star in the centre?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The star is never drawn: the eye builds it from the pacmen's mouths. Closure (D): the eye completes the gaps into a whole shape. Proximity (A): the mouths sit close together in one ring, so they are read as one group. Continuity (B): the edges of neighbouring mouths line up, and the eye carries those lines across the gaps to form the star's sides. So the answer is A, B and D.

questions.text: If the black lines represent cutting lines and dotted pink lines are folding lines, which of the options correctly represent(s) the opened up surfaces of the solid shown?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The solid is a corner staircase: 6 cubes on the floor in a 3, 2, 1 staircase with 3 cubes on top in a 2, 1 staircase, so its surface has 32 unit squares: a 6-square floor, two 5-square back walls, a 3-square top, and 13 squares on the stepped front. B and C each have exactly these faces, every one once. In A and D the flap folded off the floor at the middle step repeats the riser and step top that the upper strip already supplies, so two front squares are missing.

questions.text: Which of the following images belong(s) to Ajanta?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Ajanta's paintings use earth pigments, flowing outlines and ceiling motifs such as lotus rosettes, animals and geese among scrolls. The elephants (H, M), the geese among scrolls (K), the bulls (J) and the lotus rosette (I) are details from the Ajanta caves, so A, C and D are correct. L is in a different style and is not from Ajanta, so B is wrong.

questions.text: Based on the paintings below, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

options.label: A
options.text: These paintings use geometric grids for their construction.

options.label: B
options.text: All three painting are from Maharashtra.

options.label: C
options.text: All these paintings draw upon tribal folklore.

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: These are Warli paintings: white figures made of circles, triangles and lines on a red-brown ground. Warli art shows the tribe's village life, rituals and folklore, so C is true, and it is traditionally painted on the mud walls of houses, so D is true. The figures are drawn freehand from simple shapes, not on a geometric grid, so A is false. The Warli live in the hills on both sides of the Maharashtra and Gujarat border, so the paintings cannot be placed in Maharashtra alone, and B is not accepted.

questions.text: Which of the following is/are greenhouse gas(es)?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Carbon dioxide and methane absorb infrared radiation and trap heat in the atmosphere, so they are greenhouse gases. Hydrogen sulphide and chlorine are toxic gases but are not counted as greenhouse gases.

questions.text: Which of the options represent(s) correctly the opened up surfaces of the solid shown?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The solid is a triangular prism whose end triangles have sides 3, 4 and 5, so its faces are a 4 by 4 base, a 4 by 3 upright face, a 4 by 5 sloping face and two triangles. Check each net for exactly these faces and fold it in your mind: every triangle must sit against the edges it meets on the solid. Nets A and D fold into the prism; B and C attach a face to the wrong edge or use a wrong size.

questions.text: Consider the following text by Edward Shanken: “By 2000, it had become increasingly apparent that the exclusion and ghettoization confronting the practice and criticism of new media art and the larger historiography of art and technology required an explicit suturing strategy. In ‘Art in the Information Age’ (2001) I argued that by ‘interpreting conceptual art and art-and-technology as reflections and constituents of broad cultural transformations during the information age’ categorical distinctions can be relaxed, allowing parallels to be drawn between seemingly diverse theory of systems aesthetics and the notion of software as a metaphor for art. My analysis of works by Levine, Haacke and Kosuth in ‘Software’ led to the conclusion that in the information age, ‘meaning and value are not embedded in objects, institutions or individuals so much as they are abstracted in the production, manipulation and distribution of signs and information’. Finally, I implicitly applied Burnham’s systems approach to analyse the system by which art history is written. Using Haacke and Ascott as examples, I claimed that the historicization of an artist’s work as conceptual art or art and technology ‘says less about their work than it does about the institutional mechanisms that have created and reinforced categorical distinctions...at the expense of identifying continuities between them.” Which of the statements is/are TRUE of the paragraph above?

options.label: A
options.text: Historicization of an artist’s work speaks only of institutional mechanisms that create and define categories.

options.label: B
options.text: Categorical distinctions do not allow parallels to be drawn between seemingly diverse practices.

options.label: C
options.text: If software is a metaphor for art, meaning and value are more in the making and distribution of signs and information.

options.label: D
options.text: Conceptual art cannot be interpreted as reflections of broad cultural transformations.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Shanken says relaxing categorical distinctions allows parallels to be drawn between diverse practices, so the distinctions block such parallels (B). He concludes that meaning and value lie in the production, manipulation and distribution of signs and information (C). A is too strong: historicization says less about the work, not only about institutions. D contradicts his reading of conceptual art as reflecting cultural transformation.

questions.text: The following diagram shows the distribution of population in an apartment building as per the profession of its residents. Which of the following is/are correct?

options.label: A
options.text: Doctors and businessmen combined is less than half of the total residents.

options.label: B
options.text: About 1/3 of the population is engineers.

options.label: C
options.text: Engineers and designers combined is about 60% of the residents.

options.label: D
options.text: Doctors and businessmen combined is more than half of the total residents.

questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Measuring the slices: doctors about 20%, engineers about 33%, businessmen about 20%, designers about 27%. Doctors and businessmen together are about 40%, less than half, so A is true and D false. Engineers are about one third (B), and engineers plus designers are about 60% (C).

questions.text: In which of the following applications is a convex lens used?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A magnifying glass is a single convex lens, and a microscope uses convex objective and eyepiece lenses. A door peephole uses a concave (diverging) lens to give a wide view, and a car headlight relies on a concave mirror to make a beam.

questions.text: Who is the woman in this painting by Raja Ravi Varma?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: This is Raja Ravi Varma's 'Hamsa Damayanti': Damayanti listens to a swan carrying news of Nala. Shakuntala is shown writing to Dushyanta, Lakshmi sits on a lotus and Saraswati holds a veena, none with a messenger swan.

questions.text: Which option arranges the states in an ascending order in terms of area?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Areas: Kerala about 39,000 sq km, Gujarat about 1,96,000, Uttar Pradesh about 2,41,000 and Rajasthan about 3,42,000 (the largest state). So the ascending order is Kerala, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan.

questions.text: Shown below is a map of a city with names of prominent localities. A man starts walking from Hampalkatte towards the west, takes the second right, second left, first left, third right, second left, and walks on straight to the end of the street. Where does he reach?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Walking west from Hampalkatte, the first right is the curved ring road and the second right is the next street, heading north. Going north, the first left is the Sadashiv to Dum Dum road and the second left is the Hoskote road at the top, heading west. Its bend south is the first left. Heading south, the third right is the Navrangpura road at the bottom of the street. Going west, the second left is the road dropping south past Badi Chaudi, which runs on to Kandivali.

questions.text: The door height of entrance of an Indian Public Hall is to be finalised. Which of the following should be considered to decide the height of the door frame?

options.label: A
options.text: The height of tallest 5 percent of Indian male population.

options.label: B
options.text: The height of tallest 50 percent of Indian female population.

options.label: C
options.text: The average height of tallest 95 percent of Indian male and female population.

options.label: D
options.text: The height of tallest 95 percent of Indian male child population.

questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A door must clear almost everyone, so it is sized for the tallest users, the 95th percentile of the taller group, Indian men. That is the height of the tallest 5 percent of men. Female, child or averaged heights would leave many men hitting their heads.

questions.text: Two different views of a sphere are shown below. Select the correct digital image that is mapped on the sphere.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Match features between the two views: where the grey and black bands run, which regions are black, and how the bands meet near the poles. Then picture each flat image wrapped round the sphere, with its top and bottom edges drawn in to the poles, and compare. Image C gives the pattern seen in both views.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of traditional embroidery from Punjab?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: C is Phulkari, Punjab's embroidery of bright silk floss in geometric darn stitches. B is Lucknow's white chikankari, A is fine white leaf motifs on purple, and D is dense floral needlework of the Kashmiri kind.

questions.text: Given below is a sequence of drawings from the animation of a cricket batsman performing a pull shot, with one missing drawing represented by a question mark. Which option would best replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The sequence goes stance, then the bat coming down low across the body, then the follow-through over the shoulder. The missing frame between the stance and the downswing is the backlift, with the bat raised high behind. Only D shows the bat lifted up; A and C show the bat already swinging across, and B shows it tucked low.

questions.text: Which option will replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Read the diamond as 0 and the triangle as 1: the sums become binary, 0+0=0, 0+1=1, 1+1=10, 1+11=100 and 1+10=11. Then 10+10=100, which is triangle, diamond, diamond.

questions.text: Shown below is a flower. Which is the leaf of the plant to which the flower belongs?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: The flower is frangipani (Plumeria): five overlapping waxy white petals with a yellow centre. Its leaves are long, smooth and lance shaped with many parallel side veins, as in D. A is a maple leaf, B a three-part compound leaf, and C a broad rounded leaf.

questions.text: The word shown below s a specific font. From the options choose the letter that belongs to the same font.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Letters in the same font share their construction: the shape of the loops, the way strokes end and how the curves join, even when the weight differs. Compare each option's letter with the letters of the word. D is built the same way as the word, while A, B and C differ in the shape of their loops or the ends of their strokes.

questions.text: Which option will replace the question mark?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each figure is the previous one rotated clockwise, by 90 degrees, then 180 degrees, then 270 degrees. The next turn is 360 degrees, which leaves the shape as in the fourth figure. Only B has that shape (a row of three triangles on top with two hanging below on the left).

questions.text:
If the following operations were performed in the given sequence on the figure shown in the box, what would the resultant figure be?
i. Rotate the figure clockwise by 90 degrees.
ii. Flip along the vertical axis passing through its centre.
iii. Flip along the horizontal axis passing through its centre.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: A flip about the vertical axis followed by a flip about the horizontal axis is the same as a rotation by 180 degrees. So the three steps together are a clockwise rotation of 270 degrees, which is a 90 degree anticlockwise rotation, and the shape is not mirrored. The pentagon's flat bottom edge moves to the right side, so the shape now points left, which leaves B and D. In the original, going clockwise round the outline, each long edge ends in a spike followed by a notch; B keeps this, while D has the spikes the other way round, which is the mirror image. So the answer is B.

questions.text:
In the left column are names of some National Parks. In the right column are the names of the states in which they are located. Which option contains all correct pairs?

| | National Park | | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| i. | Jim Corbett | A. | Rajasthan |
| ii. | Ranthambore | B. | Assam |
| iii. | Kaziranga | C. | Uttarakhand |
| iv. | Kanha | D. | Madhya Pradesh |

options.label: A
options.text: Jim Corbett-Assam; Ranthambore-Rajasthan; Kaziranga-Madhya Pradesh; Kanha-Uttarakhand

options.label: B
options.text: Jim Corbett-Uttarakhand; Ranthambore-Madhya Pradesh; Kaziranga-Assam; Kanha-Rajasthan

options.label: C
options.text: Jim Corbett-Assam; Ranthambore-Rajasthan; Kaziranga-Uttarakhand; Kanha-Madhya Pradesh

options.label: D
options.text: Jim Corbett-Uttarakhand; Ranthambore-Rajasthan; Kaziranga-Assam; Kanha-Madhya Pradesh

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Jim Corbett National Park is in Uttarakhand, Ranthambore is in Rajasthan, Kaziranga (home of the one-horned rhinoceros) is in Assam and Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh. Only option D has all four pairs right. A and C put Jim Corbett in Assam, and B puts Ranthambore in Madhya Pradesh and Kanha in Rajasthan.

questions.text: Figure 1 is unfolded into Figure 2 and individual letters are written on each face. Which option is the correct representation when it is folded back?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Figure 2 is two cube nets joined at one edge: the first cube is C, A, F, B, D, E and the second is A, B, F, D, E, C. In the first cube C is folded up from A and E down from D, so C and E are opposite faces; the same holds in the second cube, where E is above D and C below A. The upper cube in every option shows E on its front face, so it cannot also show C, which rules out A, B and C. Folding the nets confirms D: the upper cube shows D on top, E in front and A on the right, and the lower cube shows A on top, C in front and B on the right, with the letters turned as in the net.

questions.text: The image below shows four different dance forms. Which states do these dance forms belong to?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Picture 1 is Kathakali, with its green face make-up, large crown and wide skirt, from Kerala. Picture 2 is Kuchipudi, from Andhra Pradesh. Picture 3 is Mohiniyattam, in the off-white and gold Kerala sari, from Kerala. Picture 4 is Sattriya, danced in the mekhela chador of Assam. This gives 1-Kerala, 2-Andhra Pradesh, 3-Kerala, 4-Assam, which is option C.

questions.text: A paper is folded in the sequence shown in the image below. Blue patches are the areas that are cut out. What would the resultant figure be when the paper is unfolded?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The sheet is folded in thirds both ways, so the final small rectangle is the middle ninth of the sheet, and each cut is copied into all nine panels, mirrored across every fold. The top-right cut sits on a fold corner and opens out into an I-shaped hole inside the sheet, and the bottom-left cut opens out into an H-shaped hole, which leaves A and B. Unfolding also gives a notch deeper at both ends on the left edge one third down, a notch with a middle tab on the top edge one third along, and notches narrow at the edge and wider inside on the bottom and right edges. Only A shows all of these.

questions.text: If the heptagon with the triangle is mirrored along the common edge (depicted by a dotted line) between two consecutive shapes, what would the resultant figure be?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: From the first heptagon to the one marked with a question mark there are six mirrorings, one across each shared edge. Tracking the corner that holds the triangle across each shared edge in turn, the triangle ends up at the lower-right corner of the last heptagon, still pointing into the shape. An even number of mirrorings gives a plain rotation, so the triangle keeps its shape. Option A has the triangle at the lower-right corner.

questions.text: Which of the following compositions is possible by rearranging pieces of Tangram puzzle (Sample given on the left)? Rotation of the pieces is allowed but flipping and scaling are not allowed.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: A tangram has seven pieces: two large triangles, one medium triangle, two small triangles, one square and one parallelogram. Since flipping is not allowed, the parallelogram must lean the same way as in the sample. Figure C uses three small triangles and only one large triangle, and figure D has two parallelograms and three small triangles, so neither can be made. In figure B the parallelogram leans the other way, so it would have to be flipped. Figure A uses exactly the seven pieces, with the parallelogram turned but not flipped.

questions.text:
Consider the poem below:

Drip drip   Drip        Drip
Dripdripdripdrip
Painters far away
Fishermen in oceans of colour

Who or what from the options, drip?
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: The poem builds a picture of paint dripping, and the people who work in oceans of colour are painters, like artists who drip paint onto a canvas. The fishermen are part of the image of colour as an ocean, not what drips. Oceans and beaches are not described as dripping at all. So the painters are the ones who drip.

questions.text: Which of the following crawl on a surface?
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Text that moves slowly across a screen, like a news ticker or film credits, is called a crawl, so words crawl on a surface. Helicopters fly, satellites orbit, and fruits do not move on their own.

questions.text:
Read the following lines from a poem:

Lad Bazaar *gallis*. Thin and crooked.
On the prime prized precincts
Sat sleeves rolled Ali
Sipping sweet *suleimani*
Props ready, goods ready
Theatre of give and take

What profession could be attributed to Ali?
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Ali sits on a prized spot in the lanes of Lad Bazaar, a market, with his goods ready, and the place is a theatre of give and take, that is buying and selling. That describes a shopkeeper. Nothing in the lines suggests teaching, flying or directing traffic.

questions.text:
Read the following lines and answer the question given below:

Pleading farts and ponderous burps
Upset the silence of dignified insides,
Sounds of occupation and exile.

What makes up dignified insides?
questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Farts and burps are sounds made by the digestive system, so the dignified insides that they disturb are the stomach and gut. Country and circus are not inside anyone, and silence is what gets upset, not what the insides are made of.

questions.text: The hour hand of a particular clock moves at half the speed, and the minute hand at 6 times the speed of a regular clock. If this strange clock matches time with the regular clock at 12 noon, what is the actual time when the strange clock next looks as shown below?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The strange clock shows the minute hand at 6 and the hour hand at about 4. Its hour hand moves at half speed, so reaching 4 takes about 8 real hours. Its minute hand moves at 6 times speed, so it makes 6 turns every real hour, one turn every 10 real minutes, and points at 6 after 5, 15, 25 minutes and so on. After 8 hours 5 minutes the minute hand has made 48.5 turns, so it points at 6, and the hour hand has moved 4 hours 2.5 minutes, just past 4. So the real time is 8.05.

questions.text: Count the number of people with a moustache in the picture below:
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Scan the crowd row by row and mark each face with hair between the nose and the upper lip, counting faces with a beard and moustache too, and tick each one off so that none is counted twice. IIT Bombay's final key gives 18.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct logo of Apple Computers?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The Apple logo has the bite taken out of the right side of the apple and the leaf tilted so that its tip points up and to the right. Option C has both. A and B have the bite on the left, and D has the leaf leaning the wrong way.

questions.text: What does a camera use to form an image?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: A camera has to form a real, inverted image on the film or sensor, and only a converging lens does that. A convex lens is a converging lens. Concave and plano-concave lenses spread light out and form only virtual images, so they cannot form an image on a screen on their own.

questions.text: The picture shows a man holding a traditional product in his hands. What is it used for?

options.label: C
options.text: Separate tea leaves from dust and foreign particles

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: The man holds a cone-shaped bamboo trap open at both ends, of the kind used in Assam and other parts of the north-east to trap fish in shallow water; he also carries a bamboo basket at his waist to keep the catch. Rice is separated from husk with a flat winnowing tray, and tea or sand is sieved, which this open cone cannot do.

questions.text:
Which of the options closely match the Avatars with their associations?

| | Avatar | | Association |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | Kurma | 1 | Karma |
| Q | Parashurama | 2 | Dharma |
| R | Rama | 3 | Complex |
| S | Krishna | 4 | Amphibian |
| T | Kalki | 5 | Destruction |
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: Kurma is the tortoise avatar, an animal of land and water, so amphibian. Parashurama is known for destroying the Kshatriya kings, so destruction. Rama is the model of righteous conduct, so dharma. Krishna teaches the path of action in the Gita, so karma, which leaves complex for Kalki. Only option C gives P-4, Q-5, R-2, S-1, T-3.

questions.text:
Which of the options correctly match the paintings with corresponding art movements?

1.Expressionism 2.Realism 3.Pop Art 4.Pointilism 5.Op Art 6.Surrealism
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: L is Edvard Munch's The Scream, the best-known Expressionist painting. J is a dark, lifelike portrait by Gustave Courbet, a Realist. I, a comic-style eye with a tear and Ben-Day dots, is Pop Art in the manner of Roy Lichtenstein. K, a Seurat bathing scene, stands for Pointillism. M, made of wavy parallel lines that trick the eye, is Op Art, and H, with its dreamlike objects, is Surrealist. That gives 1-L, 2-J, 3-I, 4-K, 5-M, 6-H, option C.

questions.text: If the following self portraits by Picasso are arranged in chronological order starting with the earliest painting, which one of these options is correct?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: C is the realistic portrait Picasso painted as a teenager in 1896. B, in deep blue, is from his Blue Period of 1901. D, with its mask-like face and heavy outlines, is from 1907, the time of Les Demoiselles d'Avignon. A, a rough drawing of a skull-like face, was made in 1972, the year before he died. So the order is C, B, D, A.

questions.text: Where is this famous painting from?
questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: This is The Great Wave off Kanagawa, a woodblock print by the Japanese artist Hokusai, with Mount Fuji small in the background. It belongs to Japan's ukiyo-e tradition, not to Korean, Chinese or Indonesian art.

questions.text: Two men start at the same point, walk in opposite directions for 4 meters, turn left and walk another 3 meters. What is the distance between them?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Let one man walk east and the other west. After turning left, the first walks north and the second walks south. They end 4 + 4 = 8 meters apart east to west and 3 + 3 = 6 meters apart north to south, so the distance is \( \sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10 \) meters.

questions.text: Which is the appropriate option that can replace the question mark to complete the series?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: In each row the third figure is the first two figures overlapped. In the hexagon row the line that is on the left of the first hexagon and the line on the right of the second both end up inside the overlap, so the second figure sits on the left and the first on the right. Doing the same with the triangles puts the downward triangle on the left and the upward triangle on the right, overlapping. Option D shows this; C has the upward triangle on the left, B overlaps them exactly, and A only puts them side by side.

questions.text: Which is the appropriate option that can replace the question mark to complete the series?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Follow each symbol along a row. The circle moves one cell clockwise round the border each time, and when it lands on another symbol's cell it is hidden, as in the third figure of the first row. In the last row the triangle goes from top-left to top-right, so next it goes to bottom-right; the star moves diagonally from bottom-left to the centre, so next it goes to top-right; the circle goes from top-right to middle-right, so next it reaches bottom-right under the triangle. That leaves a star at top-right and a triangle at bottom-right, which is option C.

questions.text: Which of the following options is related to the phrase 'Easy to understand'?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Usability is how easily people can understand and use a product. Functionality is what the product can do, durability is how long it lasts, and aesthetics is how it looks.

questions.text: Which of the following options helps in establishing interchangeability of products?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Parts can replace one another only if they are made to the same agreed sizes and specifications, which is standardization, for example a standard bulb holder or screw thread. Stylization changes how a product looks, and diversification creates more varieties, which works against interchangeability, so D is wrong too.

questions.text: The figure shows a solid formed by the union of two solids. The first is an elliptic cylinder (cylinder with an elliptical cross-section) of shorter width 4 inches, larger width 5 inches, and height of 11 inches, and the second is a cuboid of 8 inches x 5 inches x 6 inches. The centre of the extruded ellipse is aligned with the edge of the cuboid as shown in the figure. If the resultant solid is cut by a plane (shown by the red dotted line), what will be the cross section of the resulting face as viewed from an angle perpendicular to the face?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Find where the cutting plane meets each solid. It crosses the cuboid, giving a rectangle, and it cuts the elliptic cylinder at a slant. The plane rises 3 for every 4 across, so it stretches the cylinder's 4-inch width to 4 x 5/4 = 5 inches, equal to the other width, and the cut through the cylinder is a circle. Option A shows the rectangle and the circle.

questions.text: A matrix sequence is shown on the left. Which of the options given on the right can replace the matrix with question marks?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The same reshuffle turns matrix 1 into 2 and matrix 2 into 3. The new first row is the old row 1 entries 2 and 3, followed by row 2 entry 3; the new second row is the old row 1 entry 1, followed by row 3 entries 2 and 3; the new third row is the old row 2 entry 1, row 3 entry 1 and row 2 entry 2. Applying it to matrix 3 (3 9 5, 6 1 2, 7 4 8) gives 9 5 2, 3 4 8, 6 7 1, which is option B.

questions.text: What does “carbon footprint” refer to?

options.label: A
options.text: The amount of carbon dioxide produced by a certain human activity.

options.label: B
options.text: The total greenhouse gases produced by a certain human activity.

options.label: C
options.text: Geographical mapping of the amount of carbon fixed from carbon dioxide by plants through photosynthesis.

options.label: D
options.text: The measuring of the presence of prehistoric life based on the fossilised carbon content.

questions.subject: Environment and Society
questions.solution: A carbon footprint is the total amount of greenhouse gases, such as carbon dioxide and methane, released by an activity, person or product, usually given as carbon dioxide equivalent. Option A is too narrow because it counts carbon dioxide alone. C describes carbon uptake by plants and D describes carbon dating of fossils, neither of which is a footprint.

questions.text: Which is the correct top view for the solid shown?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: In plan the solid is a long strip with a pointed left end. The pointed part carries two top faces: a sloping triangle at the tip and then a steep face that ends exactly where the point widens to full width, so a line crosses the pointed part before the full-width strip starts. Along the strip the top view then shows a line at the bottom of the V, a line at the top of the curved face, and a line where the curve meets the flat foot at the right end. Option A has all of these, with spacings that match the solid: B and D miss the foot line, and C and D have no line inside the pointed part.
